title: Autolaunched, scheduled, platform-event-triggered, and orchestration concepts
objectives: Match autolaunched, schedule-triggered, platform-event-triggered, and orchestration starts to official Help trigger tables.
Explain that autolaunched no-trigger flows run in the background without screens or choices, and can be called by buttons, other flows, or Apex.
Describe schedule-triggered batch runs and $Record, and when Help points to Batch Apex instead.
Contrast platform-event-triggered Flow (async, separate transaction) with Flow Orchestration (coordinate multiple flows and teams).
diagnostic_question: You need a button that runs background updates, a nightly membership reminder, a reaction when a printer publishes an event, and a hiring process across HR and Finance. Before reading, which of autolaunched, scheduled, platform-event, orchestration, validation, or Apex owns each piece?
definition: Not every Flow starts from a screen or a record save. Autolaunched flows run in the background when a button, another flow, or Apex calls them. Schedule-triggered flows run at a specified time and frequency for a batch of records. Platform event-triggered flows start when an event message is received. Flow Orchestration coordinates multiple flows and assigns work to teams. ([Which automation tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm); [Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm); [Subscribe to Platform Event Messages with Flows](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_subscribe_flow.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who put screens on an autolaunched flow, who use a validation rule as a nightly job, or who confuse orchestration with a single approval. Choosing the start is as important as choosing Flow versus Apex.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a city transit system. Autolaunched Flow is an on-demand shuttle you radio from a button, another route, or Apex. Schedule-triggered Flow is the midnight bus that stops at every matching record. Platform-event Flow is radio dispatch when a sensor (event) fires. Orchestration is a multi-crew construction project that assigns stages to HR, Finance, and hiring. A formula is the printed timetable, validation is the inspector who will not let an illegal bus leave the depot, and approval is a human dispatcher. Batch Apex is the freight train when the midnight bus cannot carry the volume.
deeper_explanation: Which-tool trigger table: custom button or link that starts background work → Autolaunched; called by another flow → Autolaunched or Screen; called by Apex → Autolaunched; specified time and frequency → Schedule-Triggered; platform event message received → Platform Event-Triggered; coordinate multiple flows across teams → Flow Orchestration. ([Which automation tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm))

Flow Types: Autolaunched No Trigger runs in the background and does not support screens, local actions, choices, or choice sets. Schedule-Triggered launches at a specified time and frequency for each record in a batch and also does not support user interaction or screens. Platform Event Triggered launches when a platform event occurs, in the background. Orchestration types exist for multi-step, multi-user processes. ([Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm))

Triggered Flows: a schedule-triggered flow starts at the specified time and frequency for a batch of records; configure it on the Start element of your autolaunched flow; $Record gives each interview the record's field values. Record-triggered scheduled paths are a different offset on a save, not this type. ([Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm); [Schedule-Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_schedule.htm))

Platform Events developer guide: create a platform event-triggered flow from the Start element. Interviews run asynchronously in a separate transaction from the publisher; a flow can receive a batch of up to 200 event messages; order within a batch follows replay Id. Debug logs appear under Automated Process, but CreatedById/LastModifiedById use the publishing user. If an event fails, the flow does not start and no flow error email is sent. If flows, paused interviews, and processes subscribe to the same event, order is not guaranteed. ([Subscribe with Flows](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_subscribe_flow.htm))

Complementary tools: Batch Apex when you must process more records than scheduled-triggered flows allow (Help's example class of problem: 600,000 contacts); Apex for CPU-intensive work. Validation rules and formula fields are not start mechanisms. Approvals route people; orchestration coordinates flows and teams. Flow Approval Processes do not consume orchestration runs (AUTO-001).

mental_model.analogy: City transit: autolaunched is an on-demand shuttle, schedule-triggered is the midnight bus, platform-event is radio dispatch from a sensor, orchestration is a multi-crew construction project.

where_it_breaks: One Salesforce transaction can still mix record-triggered Flow and Apex (AUTO-003 / APEX-009).
Scheduled paths on record-triggered Flow are not the midnight bus type.
The 200-message batch and 600,000-contact figures are documented examples/caps to reverify, not your org's guarantee.
Orchestration credits are a neighboring billing concern; Help says Flow Approval Processes do not consume them.

claims.claim: Autolaunched flows start from a custom button/link, another flow, or Apex, run in the background, and do not support screens, local actions, choices, or choice sets.

Schedule-triggered flows run at a specified time and frequency for a batch of records without user interaction. $Record exposes each record. Batch Apex is the complementary tool when volume exceeds scheduled-triggered Flow.

Platform event-triggered flows start when an event is received, run asynchronously in a separate transaction, can batch up to 200 messages, log under Automated Process while DML user fields follow the publisher, and send no flow error email if the event never starts the flow.

claims.claim: Flow Orchestration coordinates multiple flows and assigns them to multiple teams or individuals (Help's hiring-process example).
claims.validation: Complementary tools and Get Started with Flow Orchestration.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Autolaunched is background, no screens, started by button, subflow, or Apex. Scheduled is a clock batch with $Record. Platform-event is async on the event bus. Orchestration coordinates multiple flows and teams. Validation is not a start. Batch Apex covers volume scheduled Flow cannot.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick the start from Help's table, not from habit. I never put choices on an autolaunched no-trigger flow. I do not use a scheduled Flow as a validation rule or an approval. If the nightly job is bigger than scheduled Flow allows, I say Batch Apex. Platform-event interviews are a different transaction from the publisher, which is why debug sits under Automated Process while CreatedById is the publisher.

terminology.plain: A background flow with no screens.
terminology.precise: No-trigger autolaunched type: launched by button, link, another flow, Apex, API, or orchestration. No screens, local actions, choices, or choice sets.
terminology.non_example: A screen Flow the user clicks Next on.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record-triggered: a different start, still can be background.
terminology.boundary: Subflow children are often this type.

terminology.plain: A flow that runs on a clock for a batch of records.
terminology.precise: Once, daily, or weekly at a specified time for records that meet filter criteria. No user interaction. $Record is each record.
terminology.example: Every Saturday, email LAB_ memberships about to expire.
terminology.non_example: A scheduled path on a record-triggered Flow (offset after a save).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Batch Apex: complementary when volume exceeds this type.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent unofficial batch size numbers.

terminology.plain: The record for the current scheduled (or record-triggered) interview.
terminology.precise: Triggered Flows: $Record gives each schedule-triggered interview its record field values.
terminology.example: Update LAB_ Membership Stage from $Record in the nightly flow.
terminology.non_example: A screen Flow recordId input is a different contract.
terminology.boundary: Schedule type vs record-triggered $Record share the name with different starts.

terminology.plain: A flow that starts when a platform event message is received.
terminology.precise: Background. Async separate transaction. Up to 200 messages per batch. Debug under Automated Process; DML user fields follow the publisher. Failed events do not start the flow or email a flow error.
terminology.example: Printer out-of-ink event creates a LAB_ Case.
terminology.non_example: Change Data Capture is a neighboring event family—confirm the event type.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Paused interviews can also resume on events.
terminology.boundary: Order vs other subscribers is not guaranteed.

terminology.plain: A multi-step, multi-user coordinator of flows.
terminology.precise: Help: coordinate multiple flows and assign them to multiple teams; hiring example. Distinct from a single autolaunched flow and from approval processes.
terminology.example: HR, Finance, and hiring each run different flows in sequence.
terminology.non_example: Classic Approval Processes on one object.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Evaluation autolaunched flows for orchestration conditions are a neighboring type.

terminology.plain: The complementary programmatic batch when scheduled Flow cannot cover volume.
terminology.precise: Help: perform an operation for more records than scheduled-triggered flows allow, example updating 600,000 contacts.
terminology.example: Nightly update of a documented huge Contact set.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Queueable Apex: a different async type (APEX-011).
terminology.boundary: Do not treat 600,000 as your org's cap.

terminology.plain: A time offset on a record-triggered Flow, not schedule-triggered type.
terminology.precise: Part of the flow runs after the triggering save, e.g. three days later.
terminology.example: Follow-up email three days after LAB_ Quote create.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Platform event wait/pause: another delay mechanism.
terminology.boundary: AUTO-003 introduced this; do not collapse types.

terminology.plain: The user shown on debug logs for platform event-triggered interviews.
terminology.precise: Logs appear under Automated Process, but the interview runs in the context of the publishing user for CreatedById and LastModifiedById.
terminology.example: Debug log named Automated Process after a PE publish.
terminology.non_example: The running user of a screen Flow.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Without sharing vs this log name: different topics.
terminology.boundary: Do not assume CRUD as Automated Process without checking publisher context.

when_to_use: Use an autolaunched Flow when a button, another Flow, or Apex must run background work with no screens.
Use a schedule-triggered Flow when a clock should process a filtered batch via $Record, such as daily membership reminders.
Use a platform-event-triggered Flow when a platform event message should start background automation in a separate transaction.
Use Flow Orchestration when multiple flows and teams must be coordinated, not when a validation rule or a single approval would suffice.
Use Batch Apex when the batch is larger than scheduled-triggered Flow can handle, and Apex for CPU-intensive work—not as the default shuttle.
when_not_to_use: Do not use an autolaunched Flow when a person must complete screens—that is a screen Flow.
Do not use a schedule-triggered Flow as a substitute for a validation rule that must block illegal saves.
Do not use a platform-event Flow when a record save should start the work—that is record-triggered (AUTO-003).
Do not use Flow Orchestration when you only need a formula field, a validation rule, or one approval process.
Do not use Apex or Batch Apex for a small nightly reminder a schedule-triggered Flow can send.
configuration_or_code_location: New Flow → Autolaunched, Schedule-Triggered, Platform Event-Triggered, or Orchestration type.
Start element: schedule frequency and object filter, or platform event.
Custom button/link or Apex `Flow.Interview` / invocable launch for autolaunched.
Setup → Platform Events for the event definition (metadata), not the business rows.

interview_questions.question: Autolaunched versus screen versus schedule-triggered?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Autolaunched is background, no screens, started by button/subflow/Apex. Screen needs a person. Schedule-triggered is a clock batch with $Record.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Help's trigger table. I never put choices on no-trigger autolaunched. I do not use scheduled Flow as a validation rule or as an approval. Record-triggered remains AUTO-003 if a save should start the work.
follow_ups: Can Apex start a screen Flow?

interview_questions.question: When do you pick platform-event-triggered Flow?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a platform event message should start background work. It is not a record save and not a validation rule.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain async separate transactions, 200-message batches, Automated Process logs versus publisher CreatedById, and no flow email if the event never starts the flow. Order versus other subscribers is not guaranteed.
interview_questions.example: LAB_PrinterOutOfInk__e publishes; a platform-event-triggered Flow creates a LAB_ Case in a later transaction.
weak_answer_warnings: Expecting it in the publisher's trigger

interview_questions.question: Nightly job must touch more contacts than scheduled Flow can. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Help's complementary tool is Batch Apex when volume exceeds scheduled-triggered Flow. I do not invent a number beyond Help's 600,000-contact example class of problem.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I first ask whether filters can shrink the batch. I do not use a validation rule or a formula as a batch engine. I may still use Flow plus invocable Apex if only one step is code.
interview_questions.example: Updating a documented huge LAB_ Contact set nightly.

interview_questions.question: Hiring across HR, Finance, and hiring team. Orchestration or approval?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If each team runs different flows as stages, that is Flow Orchestration. If one record needs a human accept/reject, that is an approval process.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not replace a PTO approval with orchestration, or a nightly email with orchestration. AUTO-001 already said Flow Approval Processes do not consume orchestration runs.
interview_questions.example: Multi-stage LAB_ hiring versus LAB_ PTO approval.

interview_questions.question: Why not a validation rule for the midnight membership email?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Validation True means invalid save. A reminder is communication on a legal record. That is schedule-triggered Flow (or after-save), not validation.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: A formula might display days-to-expiry but will not send the email. Apex is unnecessary for a modest batch. Approval is a human decision, not a reminder.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Membership expiry email at 30 days.
weak_answer_warnings: Validation that 'emails' in the error text

interview_questions.question: Apex should launch a Flow after Opportunity stage changes. Which type?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Autolaunched. Which-tool: called by Apex code → Autolaunched. A screen Flow would wait for a person who is not there.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still ask whether a record-triggered Flow could do it without Apex. If Apex already exists, it can start the autolaunched interview. I pass input variables explicitly; there is no recordId action contract unless a Flow action is used.
follow_ups: How do you test the interview?

interview_questions.question: PE Flow never runs and nobody got a flow error email.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If the event failed, the flow never started, so Help says no flow error email. Debug the platform event, subscriber, and that the Start element selects that event.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not look only at Flow fault emails. I do not 'fix' it with a validation rule. I remember other subscribers may interleave.

interview_questions.question: Transit analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Shuttle is autolaunched, midnight bus is scheduled, radio is platform event, construction crew is orchestration, freight train is Batch Apex. It breaks because scheduled paths on record-triggered Flow are not the midnight bus type, and one save still has AUTO-003 rooms.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Validation is the inspector, formula the printed timetable, approval a human dispatcher. I never use a labeled-drawer story.
interview_questions.example: Someone designing a scheduled path thinking they created a schedule-triggered Flow.
follow_ups: Where does Data Cloud trigger sit?
